dataSource.fetchedBy: research agent, verified against the official source
dataSource.notes:
SOURCING: All numbers come from chick-fil-a.com — the /nutrition-allergens guide plus individual /menu/... item pages, which are server-rendered (not JS-gated) and expose full macro panels. Note the lead URL chick-fil-a.com/nutrition is a 404; the live path is /nutrition-allergens.

CROSS-VALIDATION: I pulled 7 items from BOTH the aggregate nutrition guide and their individual item pages (Spicy Chicken Sandwich, Deluxe Sandwich, Chicken Biscuit, Hash Brown Scramble Bowl, Egg White Grill, Hash Browns, Fruit Cup). All 7 agreed exactly on all four macros, which is why I was willing to take Spicy Deluxe Sandwich and Grilled Chicken Club from the guide page alone — those two are the only items here not confirmed on their own item page.

REVERSE-ENGINEERED ITEMS (3): Chick-fil-A's salad pages state literally "Nutrition values are per Salad (includes toppings and dressing)" and show an "Includes" line itemizing the dressing's calories. So the published salad totals are COMPOSED numbers, not line items. I subtracted the dressing packet to get dressing-free bases:
  - Side Salad: 470/6/14/42 minus Avocado Lime Ranch (310/1/3/32) = 160/5/11/10
  - Cobb Salad: 830/41/31/60 minus Avocado Lime Ranch (310/1/3/32) = 520/40/28/28
  - Market Salad: 550/28/42/31 minus Zesty Apple Cider Vinaigrette (230/0/16/19) = 320/28/26/12
Two of these three (Side Salad 160/5/11/10 and Cobb 520/40/28/28) land exactly on Chick-fil-A's own separately-published dressing-free values, which is what gave me confidence the subtraction is the right model rather than a coincidence. The three salads are therefore also shipped as presets, where component sums reproduce the published totals exactly.

COOL WRAP CAVEAT — read before trusting: the Cool Wrap's published 660/43/32/45 is listed under a plain "Amount per serving" header with NO "Includes" dressing breakdown, unlike the salads. Subtracting Avocado Lime Ranch from it would yield 350/42/29/13, which happens to match the known dressing-free wrap — but because the page does not declare dressing is inside the total, I did NOT decompose it and shipped the published 660 as-is. Consequence: if a user adds a dressing to a Cool Wrap in the builder, they may double-count. Treat Cool Wrap as "as served" and consider suppressing the dressings station for it.

PORTION BASIS: Dipping sauces are 1 oz containers; salad dressings are 2 oz packets (both per the source). Waffle Fries are the medium serving (the only size the item page publishes). Nuggets/Strips are per stated piece count. Chick-fil-A does not publish gram weights on these pages, so serving descriptions use the count/size language the source itself uses.

CATEGORY IDS: Reused existing vocabulary throughout — entrees, mains (salad bases), sides, dips (1 oz dipping sauces, so the 3-scoop cap applies naturally), dressings (2 oz packets, 2-cap). I invented ONE new id, "breakfast", because it is a genuinely separate daypart station and nothing in the vocabulary honestly covers biscuits/burritos/parfaits.
